claim.why_it_matters: Two sub-entries (of Flagging and warning mechanisms) are merged into one line.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (PDF p868, printed folio 846) shows, at the top of the right column, two separate indented index sub-entries continuing 'Flagging and warning mechanisms' from the left column: 'Prototype versus repository 145' and, on its own line below, 'Syntax violations 3'. The markdown (page-868.md line 62) puts both on one line, 'Prototype versus repository 145 Syntax violations 3', with no hard break, while the preceding sub-entries end in a backslash line break. Both entries and their page numbers are present and correctly quoted, so no text is lost. The entry boundary is lost, though, and the merged line reads as one entry. That is a structural defect in the index's entry structure, beyond simple reflow. It does not affect normative content.
